newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on commercial, export demand.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on commercial, export demand.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on commercial, crusher and exporter demand, traders said.
"Cargill bought August and November, crushers bought August, exporters bought November and there were farmer hedges," a trader said.
November WCE futures crush margin rose to -4.64 Wednesday from -7.02 Tuesday. July-Aug spread to $11 from $10.

August canola futures rose $4.60 to close at $351.70 and November ended up $2.10 at $342.70. July flax ended $1.10 higher at $340 on commercial short covering linked to low stocks while November lost $0.80 to end at $283. July-Sep spread at $55, Sep-Nov $5. Feed peas did not trade.

July western barley rose $4.60 to $124.60 on commission short covering, October rose $2 to $124.50 on local and commission demand and scale up hedges with 100 late hedges. Volume was 675 lots. July-Oct spread at even money.
Local and commercial buying brought October feed wheat up $1.50 to $145.60, December up $2.20 to $150.70. Volume 558.
Commercials and commission houses bought December oats up US$2 to US$107.50. Volume was 45 lots.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except oats, peas.)
